- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2 points in next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.5 points to forecast for next 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.3.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5 in first 3 days.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), model fails to capture volatility — apply smoothing or lagged sentiment weighting to avoid overfitting.  
- If true outcome is consistently lower than forecast in last 5 days, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports upside.
